faults.title: No fault at all
faults.proves: that the harness fails loudly when nothing was actually broken
faults.doesNotProve: anything about the controls — this run exercises the guard, not the system

faults.title: Flare over-reports escrowed funds
faults.proves: that C3 detects Flare accounting for escrow the XRP Ledger does not hold, using two sources that cannot move each other
faults.doesNotProve: that C3 would catch a shortfall introduced on the XRPL side instead

faults.title: Flare under-reports escrowed funds
faults.proves: that C3 is two-sided — unrecorded escrow is a breach, not a conservative rounding
faults.doesNotProve: that the direction of a real discrepancy could be inferred from the exception alone

faults.title: Flare claims more spendable XRP than the vault holds
faults.proves: that C4 detects a liquid shortfall after the ledger's own reserve
faults.doesNotProve: that a surplus is safe — C4 deliberately treats excess as an observation

faults.title: XRPL silently drops one escrow object
faults.proves: that C3 catches a data source that returns a well-formed, plausible, incomplete answer — the failure mode that produces a confident wrong verdict rather than an error
faults.doesNotProve: that a dropped object would be noticed if Flare's figure were stale in the same direction

faults.title: XRPL replays a stale balance
faults.proves: that C4 does not accept a balance that is plausible but too small to cover the claim
faults.doesNotProve: that a stale balance LARGER than the truth would be detected — it would not

faults.title: XRPL is unreachable
faults.proves: that losing the independent source produces DISCLAIMER rather than CLEAN — the single easiest way for an assurance product to become dishonest is to score missing evidence as a pass
faults.doesNotProve: that partial evidence is handled correctly; this is the total-loss case

faults.title: An escrow is denominated in something other than XRP
faults.proves: that an un-summable escrow disclaims instead of counting as zero, which would manufacture a shortfall the moment a newer amendment ships
faults.doesNotProve: that the non-XRP amount could be reconciled — only that we refuse to guess it

faults.title: The destination allowlist is emptied
faults.proves: that C2 catches a precondition failure that would make C1 pass vacuously
faults.doesNotProve: that C1 itself is correct — only that its preconditions are checked

knownUncaught.title: XRPL reports a balance LARGER than the truth
knownUncaught.why: C4 only breaches when the claim exceeds spendable, so an inflated balance makes the vault look healthier and is not detected. Catching it needs a third source we do not have.

knownUncaught.title: Flare and XRPL are BOTH wrong in the same direction
knownUncaught.why: A cross-source reconciliation cannot detect a discrepancy that does not exist between its two sources. This is the structural limit of the method, not an implementation gap.

knownUncaught.title: A control asserts the wrong invariant entirely
knownUncaught.why: Fault injection proves a control CAN fire, never that it is asking the right question. Our own 93 retracted defaults fired correctly against a request that asked for the wrong amount.
